author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows under its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name. It is the inverse view of the veterinarian directory, served on one page at its own address.
acceptance_criteria: the directory is served at the address /specialties.html, reachable by that address alone
every specialty the clinic knows is listed under its stored name
all specialties render on one page, with no division into pages
each specialty shows the veterinarians holding it by full name, first name then last name, as in "Helen Leary"
a specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed and shown as held by none
a veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page
a clinic that knows no specialties still yields a rendered page that lists none
two specialties stored under the same name each appear as their own entry
specialties, and the veterinarians under each, are presented in a stable order across requests
nothing on the page offers to add, change, or remove a specialty or a veterinarian
no navigation entry and no link from another page leads to the directory
the page carries the navigation every page carries, per REQ-SYS-001
any wording the page introduces is present in every supported language, per REQ-LANG-002
non_goals: managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2 unchanged)
a navigation entry or a link from another page to the directory
listing veterinarians who hold no specialty
searching or filtering the directory (NG-9 unchanged)
notes: Existing message keys already cover specialties, name and none; add wording only if the page needs new text, and then in every supported language. Three open questions stay open in docs/prd.md and the slice does not depend on them: a visible entry point (deferred to a possible follow-up), the ordering key behind the stable-order edge case, and whether same-named specialties should merge. The narrow reading is recorded as edge cases 2 and 3.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory lives in the existing vet feature package and needs one design element the codebase has never had: a read view running against the direction of the Vet-to-Specialty mapping. Vet owns the many-to-many; Specialty holds no back-reference, and VetRepository therefore cannot reach a specialty no veterinarian holds. Two new types close that gap, both matching in-force catalog patterns. SpecialtyRepository is a Repository over the Specialty lookup value, mirroring PetTypeRepository. SpecialtyDirectory is an immutable value object that pairs each stored specialty with the veterinarians holding it, assembled by a static factory over the two collections. VetController gains a third route that binds nothing, delegates, and selects a view — no business rule joins it. docs/system-design.md Contracts now carries the route, the two new rows, and the ordering guarantee; ADR 2026-08-24-specialty-directory-as-a-derived-read-model records the rejected inverse-association alternative.
integration_points: VetController gains a GET /specialties.html handler taking no request parameter, returning view vets/specialtyList

VetController's constructor gains a SpecialtyRepository argument alongside VetRepository — every existing @WebMvcTest(VetController.class) test needs the new bean present or the context fails to start
SpecialtyDirectory reads the cached VetRepository.findAll() collection and the uncached SpecialtyRepository result; it mutates neither
the new template calls the shared layout fragment with a menu value matching no navigation item, so no entry highlights and none is added

patterns.description: lookup-entity repository with an explicit ORDER BY query — the shape SpecialtyRepository follows, except it extends the narrow Repository base (as VetRepository does) rather than JpaRepository, whose inherited write methods would contradict NG-2
controller handler shape: take the model, populate attributes, return a view name; the specialty handler does the same with no page parameter and no pagination attributes
template shape: layout fragment call, th:text on every visible string, #{none} for an empty holder list, first-name-then-last-name rendering for a veterinarian
sorted-projection accessor over an unordered persisted Set — the precedent for ordering a collection in code rather than in the mapping

risks.risk: BaseEntity declares no equals or hashCode, so specialty instances compare by object identity. Vet instances come from the vets cache while specialties come from a fresh query, so the two sources hold different objects for the same row.
risks.mitigation: Match veterinarians to specialties on getId(), never on object identity and never on name. Name matching would also merge the same-named specialties that edge case 2 requires to stay separate.

risks.risk: The vets cache hands out shared Vet instances across requests; mutating one, or its specialty set, would corrupt later reads.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory reads only. It copies the collections it is handed and exposes unmodifiable views; it never sorts a live collection in place.

risks.risk: Adding a SpecialtyRepository constructor argument to VetController breaks the existing @WebMvcTest slice tests before the new test is written.
risks.mitigation: Extend the existing setup in VetControllerTests with the new collaborator in the same step that adds the constructor argument.

risks.risk: The page renders every specialty and every veterinarian with no size bound, and pagination is a recorded non-goal.
risks.mitigation: Accepted at seed-data scale and recorded in the ADR's Consequences. Nothing in this slice may add a page parameter.

risks.risk: A record type reached from a Thymeleaf expression may need a reflection hint under GraalVM native image; the standard gate does not build one.
risks.mitigation: If the native build fails on property access, register SpecialtyDirectory and its entry type in PetClinicRuntimeHints. Not a blocker for this slice.

risks.risk: I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails any HTML line carrying literal text without a th:text attribute, and any new key missing from one of the eleven bundles.
risks.mitigation: Reuse the existing keys specialties, vets, name, and none where they fit; add any genuinely new key to all eleven bundles in the same step.

notes: Verdict is new rather than minor because the slice introduces the codebase's first derived read model and a decision with a reasonable rejected alternative — a mappedBy inverse collection on Specialty, which would cycle through the /vets serialization route and widen the Vet aggregate for a read-only page. Narrow readings taken where the PRD's open questions leave design to decide: (1) ordering — specialties by name then id, veterinarians by last name, first name, then id, following the ORDER BY name precedent in PetTypeRepository and the name-sorted accessor on Vet; the id tiebreaker is what makes the order total when two specialties share a name; (2) same-named specialties — matched by identity, so each stays its own entry, per PRD edge case 2; (3) visible entry point — none, and the layout fragment is not touched. Test placement: the four data-shape behaviors (every specialty by stored name, unheld specialty, veterinarian holding none omitted, empty clinic) are decidable in SpecialtyDirectoryTests with real objects and no mocks, which moves them to the base of the pyramid; the two rendering behaviors (full name, single page) belong in VetControllerTests against the rendered page. The prd-entry's file_targets do not name SpecialtyDirectoryTests — it is added here as a primary path, not a substitution. No cache annotation on SpecialtyRepository: open question 5 in system-design.md flags the vets cache as having no eviction, and a second uncached-invalidation surface should not be added under this slice.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Output escaping: specialtyList.html renders every data-derived value through th:text (entry.specialty.name, vet.firstName/lastName) and static labels through th:text=#{...}; no th:utext, th:inline, th:onclick, javascript: URL, or th:href/th:src carrying user data anywhere in the new template. A grep sweep of the whole templates tree confirms no unescaped-output construct was introduced by this slice, so the Thymeleaf-default escaping mitigation in docs/system-design.md#threat-model still holds unbroken.

JPQL construction: SpecialtyRepository.findAll uses a single compile-time constant @Query string with no parameters, no bind variables, no SPEL and no concatenation; the ORDER BY targets fixed entity properties, not a caller-supplied sort key. No injection sink exists on the new read path, and the handler takes no request parameters at all (no @RequestParam, @PathVariable, @RequestBody, or Model attribute binding), so there is no attacker-controlled input reaching the query.

Cache safety: SpecialtyDirectory.of only reads the @Cacheable("vets") collection. It iterates the collection and each Vet.getSpecialties() without calling any mutator, accumulates into locally allocated HashMap/ArrayList, and both record constructors defensively List.copyOf their component. No sort-in-place on the shared list (stream().sorted() copies), no add/remove/clear against the cached collection or against any Specialty/Vet entity, so no cross-request poisoning of the shared cache entry is reachable through this path.

Exposure surface: GET /specialties.html serves the identical vet-and-specialty dataset already published unauthenticated by the existing /vets.html and /vets routes. It adds no new class of data to the unauthenticated surface and no new mutating route. The absence of authentication is a pre-existing, documented posture (docs/system-design.md#security-context), not something this change alters; per the review contract, pre-existing concerns are not re-raised here.

Supply chain and configuration: the change set touches no build file, no properties file, no actuator or datasource configuration, and adds no dependency, so no new CVE surface enters the tree and no dependency-resolution check applies to this slice. A sweep of the added lines for credential-shaped material (password, secret, token, api key, credential) returns nothing; the new code holds no literal values beyond JPQL identifiers and message-bundle keys.

question:
Please apply the amendment below to docs/testing-principles.md, and confirm the CLAUDE.md follow-up.

DECISION. A framework slice test's excluded beans are boundary substitutions, not internal mocks. Grounding: docs/architecture-principles.md names the repository 'the default persistence boundary' (Building Blocks table), so a repository sits on the sanctioned side of the brief's mock-only-at-system-boundaries rule. The rule does not rest on how wide the interface is -- SpecialtyRepository exposes one findAll(), so a hand-written fake was feasible here, and the rule still permits the stub. What it rests on is where the boundary sits.

PROPOSED TEXT for docs/testing-principles.md, section 'Mocking Policy'. Insert after the paragraph beginning 'Mock-framework stubs are tolerated, not encouraged.' and before the paragraph beginning 'If a test needs more lines of setup than assertion':

----- begin -----
**A framework slice test's excluded beans are boundary substitutions, not internal mocks.** A web-slice test loads the web layer alone, so the persistence gateways its subject depends on cannot be real. `architecture-principles.md` names the repository the default persistence boundary, which puts those beans on the sanctioned side of the mock-only-at-boundaries rule. A new slice test may stand them in with the framework's bean-override stub, and owes no exception rationale for doing so.

Two bounds hold:

| Bound | Rule |
|-------|------|
| **Supply data, never behavior** | A stub returns fixture data. A stub that encodes a rule the production code owns -- ordering, filtering, derivation -- moves the specification into the test. That rule gets a unit test on the type that owns it. |
| **One style per class** | A test class substitutes all of its excluded beans the same way. Mixing a hand-written fake and a framework stub across one slice costs more than either choice saves. |

Outside a slice test the hierarchy is unchanged: real implementation first, hand-written double next, framework stub as a conscious exception. The project's `CLAUDE.md` names the concrete slice annotation and stub mechanism for this stack.
----- end -----

The text is deliberately stack-neutral, matching the brief's opening rule that the principles are language-agnostic and the concrete harness is named in CLAUDE.md (the same delegation the existing 'one sanctioned mock' paragraph uses).

Applied to the finding: VetControllerTests's @MockitoBean SpecialtyRepository is permitted outright under this rule, not a tolerated exception. Both bounds hold there -- the stub returns fixture specialties and encodes no ordering (SpecialtyDirectory owns ordering and is unit-tested for it), and the class now substitutes both excluded repositories the same way.

CLAUDE.md: YES, a correction is required, and NO, it does not belong in this slice.

Why required: CLAUDE.md:60 reads '**No mocks**: All tests use real value objects and real I/O. No Mockito or mock libraries.' That is already false today -- VetControllerTests has carried @MockitoBean VetRepository since before this slice, and testing-principles.md sanctions the web harness and tolerates existing framework stubs. My rule widens the contradiction from tolerating old stubs to permitting new ones, which CLAUDE.md:60 flatly forbids. Two edits: (1) replace the flat 'No mocks' claim with a pointer to the brief's hierarchy (real first, hand-written double next, framework stub at a boundary or as a conscious exception); (2) name the concrete mechanisms for this stack -- MockMvc/@WebMvcTest as the sanctioned harness and @MockitoBean as the bean-override stub -- which testing-principles.md explicitly delegates to CLAUDE.md and which is missing there today.

Why a separate slice: CLAUDE.md is outside my write scope and outside the REQ-VET-003 changeset. The doc-reviewer already routed a CLAUDE.md drift finding to a separate slice on identical reasoning (handoff.jsonl line 18: the Build Commands table and Quality Gate name formatJava/checkJavaFormat where the real tasks are format/checkFormat, shared with scripts/layout.toml:122). Fold both into one CLAUDE.md-accuracy slice, sequenced after the brief amendment lands so the stack-specific text has a brief rule to point at.
